_source: Watched in the owner's Chrome 2026-11-17: frames every ~3 s, words from YouTube's transcript panel. Our own descriptions; shots approximate from sampled frames.

hook.firstFrame: a small cartoon person planting a single flag on a flat political world map
hook.firstLine: What if the entire world suddenly became one country?

shots.picture: a cartoon person plants one flag over a colourful political world map
a cartoon guard stands on a map of Europe and Africa, borders fading
DAY 1 card over a world map covered in tiny people, a huge population counter
a cartoon citizen on a podium in front of the map
a cartoon plane flies a route across the map with a pin
DAY 2: a beach stall with a price board, a shopper puzzled
a map with a single currency figure on a card over it
a crowd at the stall pointing at a crazy price on the board
DAY 4: three politicians with speech signs over Europe
a soldier standing alone on a world map
a whip blur into a field with a rocket on a pad and a scientist
three clocks over a dark blue map, a worried leader below
Africa map with the question CAPITAL? and candidate cities
a football pitch, scoreboard WORLD vs WORLD, a trophy
back to the blue world map and the planted flag

lines.gist: the what-if question, no borders, one flag
day one: you are one of 8 billion citizens, passports useless
day two: 180 currencies gone, one world money
prices go wild; day three, an election where one in three voters is in India or China
day four: thousands of languages at the first meeting
day five: the world's military spending, now with no one to fight
day six: time zones and a capital; day seven: one thing everyone agrees on

ending.lastFrame: the blue world map with the single flag, the first frame again

whyItWorks: the title's question is the first sentence: no warm-up
a DAY counter turns the idea into a countdown the viewer wants to finish
every day is a new place with a small cartoon person doing something there
sourced figures (population, currencies, military spending) put on a sign in the scene; the end loops to the first frame
